title: reading-notes-sysml-llm-scaling-aria-thompson
content:
Quick notes from SysML 2024 session + papers I skimmed (mostly systems-focused on LLM inference). Filing as a scratchpad - rough, lots of TODOs.

High-level takeaways:
- Papers consistently emphasize joint optimization across model, kernel, and scheduler layers rather than isolated improvements. Kernel selection + request routing wins in many evaluations.
- Continuous/online batching + adaptive timeout heuristics seem to give best latency/throughput tradeoff for mixed workloads. Several groups use percentile-based time windows rather than fixed batch intervals.
- Prefix/KV cache eviction policies are super workload-dependent. LRU/recency isn't always best; frequency-aware + request-shape heuristics help for chat-heavy workloads.
- Quantization still a good win but brittle: per-layer calibration and fallback to FP16 for hallucination-sensitive prompts is recommended.
- Model variants (smaller decoders, quantized shapes) as graceful degradation path is a recurring pattern - best when routing + fallback latency budgets are known.

Notes on specific techniques & what we could try at Redwood: 
- Kernel selection by sequence-length distribution: paper suggests maintaining small histogram per model/route and picking kernels accordingly. Could integrate into our model catalog profiles (add sequence_len_hist per sample window). (See linked arXiv)
- Adaptive batching: percentile timers (p95 batch wait) rather than fixed ms yields better p99 latency. Add a config knob in Dedicated to choose wait policy: fixed / dynamic-percentile / shape-aware. -> Ticket idea: INF-523 (prototype dynamic-percentile wait policy).
- KV cache sharding: for multi-tenant GPUs, move to per-tenant KV segments to reduce cross-tenant eviction thrash. For Dedicated, allow tenant pinning to GPU pool + KV quotas.
- Quantization calibration: run small in-situ calibration on customer prompts (opt-in) to detect tokens where FP16/8 causes quality regressions; automatically mark routes that need higher-precision fallback. Privacy concern -> needs KMS + consent.

Operational notes from talks:
- Observability: trace token-level timing (kernel execution, memcopy, sync) and correlate with request-level SLO violations. We already have token-level traces, but need better aggregation dashboards (per-model, per-gpu).
- Canary rollouts for model + kernel combos: run small percent of traffic through new kernel/config and compare quality/latency - need automated rollback triggers (latency spike or quality regression on eval-set).

Open questions / things to validate:
- How much overhead does dynamic kernel switching add at runtime? Is it worth the complexity vs selecting best kernel at deploy-time? (microbench experiments needed)
- Are percentile-based timers stable under bursty traffic? Might oscillate; need dampening.
- For quantization calibration, what minimal sample size is needed to detect quality drop reliably?

Ideas for experiments (quick prototypes):
1) Small microbench: measure kernel selection benefit by feeding real request traces (past 24h) through simulator that picks kernel by sequence bucket. Compare throughput/latency vs single kernel baseline. -> small script + trace subset.
2) Batch wait policy A/B: implement dynamic-percentile waiter in serving runtime (config flag), run on canary pool for low-risk tenants for 1 week. Measure token cost, p50/p95/p99 latency.
3) KV cache eviction ablation: implement frequency-aware eviction (LFU-ish) and compare to LRU on chat-heavy tenants. Look for p99 improvements and cross-tenant interference drop.

Personal action items / TODOs:
- Share draft of experiment plans with Samira + Noah (INF-523 + INF-524).
- Add histogram-collection PR to model catalog (sequence_len_hist metric) - assign to infra team.
- Draft short proposal for "quantization-calibration-as-service" (privacy checklist + opt-in flow).

Random notes/clips from talks:
- "Kernel switching should be priced as a product feature - developer-visible knob." 
- "Failure modes matter: falling back to smaller models can be preferable to slow degraded large model."
- Slide: heatmap of batch sizes vs latency for transformer kernels - non-linear regimes where batching actually harms p99 if under-dimensioned GPU memory.

References I want to re-read:
- SysML paper (linked) on kernel selection + scheduler design.
- Preprint on online quantization calibration (arXiv link above).
- Ops talk slides from "LLM Serving at Scale" (SysML workshop) - contains useful dashboards layouts.

Notes to self / brainstorming (quick):
- Could expose an "inference profile" API to customers: per-route, show expected p50/p95 latency, cost-per-token, recommended batch policy, recommended quantization profile. Make it actionable: "flip to dynamic wait" or "enable quant-cal".
- Consider integrating small eval harness into console so customers can run their prompt set across model variants and see quality delta (lightweight evals).

Links/snippets: 
- Jira: INF-342 (kernel-telemetry), INF-523 (dynamic-batcher-prototype), INF-524 (kv-eviction-ablation).
- Slack threads: #infra-kernels-thread, #dedicated-alpha.

End of scratchpad. Will refine into a short proposal once experiment data is in.

-- Aria
